findings.title: Prisma raw queries do not support array parameters — `ANY(${teamIds})` will fail
findings.body: The new SQL conditions pass JavaScript arrays directly as raw query parameters, e.g. `Prisma.sql`("teamId" = ANY(${teamIds}))` and `("userId" = ANY(${uniqueUserIds}))` (also used for team scope at line 201). Prisma's raw query serialization does not support array values as bind parameters — passing an array into a `Prisma.sql` placeholder throws a serialization error at runtime (the documented workaround is `Prisma.join(...)` for IN-style clauses). Any code path that executes these conditions via `$queryRaw` (as the updated integration test does) will throw instead of returning results, so the org and team scopes are broken for actual query execution.

findings.title: `findMany` method removed — breaking change for existing callers
findings.body: The PR deletes the public `findMany(findManyArgs)` method and replaces it with `getBaseConditions()`, changing the service's public contract from returning typed `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` rows to returning a raw `Prisma.Sql` fragment. Nothing in this PR updates callers of `InsightsBookingService.findMany`; any existing consumer will fail to compile (and would otherwise need to hand-write raw SQL against the `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` table). Either keep a query method on the service or update all call sites in the same PR.

findings.title: Single filter condition returned unwrapped produces operator-precedence hazard when combined
findings.body: `buildFilterConditions` returns the single condition unwrapped when only one filter is present, e.g. `("eventTypeId" = X) OR ("eventParentId" = X)` without surrounding parentheses. `getBaseConditions` wraps conditions when both auth and filters exist, but the returned filter fragment is also exposed via `getFilterConditions()` and embedded unparenthesized in the eventTypeId condition itself (line 106 lacks outer parentheses). If this fragment is ever composed with another `AND` at a level that doesn't wrap it (as `conditions.reduce` in `buildFilterConditions` does wrap, but callers composing the raw SQL themselves may not), the OR will bind incorrectly and leak rows from other event types. Add explicit parentheses around the OR clause in the eventTypeId filter, e.g. `(("eventTypeId" = ${id}) OR ("eventParentId" = ${id}))`.
